sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier occurs in a major and a minor form. Major: medium-sized, the head and the first antennal segment light red-brown, the rest of the antennae ochre-brown, the thorax and abdomen deeply coloured; head shape in dorsal view variable, usually widest in the middle; nasus moderately long and stout, slightly less than 2/5 of the total head length; antennae usually 13-segmented, segment 4 the shortest of all, the mandibles without apical teeth. Compared with E. tumuli it is paler, with a stouter nasus and a different head shape. Minor: head long and narrow, distinctly constricted, the nasus narrow, the antennae 12-segmented, the mandibles with well-developed apical teeth; compared with E. pulleinei it is much darker, with different antennal segmentation; compared with E. curtus the head is much paler and the antennal segments longer; compared with E. nichollsi the head is much paler and the antennae have one segment fewer. The alate is not recorded in the original.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major: a medium-sized species, the head and the first antennal segment light red-brown, the rest of the antennae ochre-brown; the thorax and abdomen deeply coloured (ochre-brown), the abdominal sternites and femora slightly paler; tibiae and tarsi white. Head, thorax and abdomen mainly covered with microtrichia; the apical 1/3 of the nasus with similar but longer hairs, the apex of the nasus and the terminal abdominal segments with only a few slightly longer hairs. Head shape in dorsal view variable; usually widest in the middle, the sides slightly to distinctly rounded, the posterior part broadly rounded; sometimes widest at the anterior 1/3 and slightly narrowed posteriorly; sometimes appearing constricted in the middle; nasus moderately long and stout, slightly less than 2/5 of the total head length, variable in basal width; the dorsum of the head almost straight in side view, only slightly convex above the antennal insertions. Antennae usually 13-segmented; segment 2 about half of segment 1, cylindrical; segment 3 long; segment 4 the shortest of all; segment 5 slightly longer than segment 2; segments 6—9 long, almost as long as segment 3; segments 11—13 progressively shorter; segment 13 about as long as segment 2, cylindrical, obtusely pointed at the apex. In some specimens segments 3 and 4, and segments 5 and 6, are closely fused, giving a 12-segmented antenna; in others the normally long segment 3 is more or less subdivided, giving an antenna that may be counted as 14-segmented. Mandibles without apical teeth. Minor: colour as in the major, but the head long and narrow and distinctly constricted (Figs. 216, 217), the nasus narrow, the antennae 12-segmented. Segment 2 of the antenna the shortest of all; segment 3 longer than segment 2 and much narrower at the base; segments 4—11 all longer than segment 3; segment 12 about as long as segment 3, rounded at the apex. Mandibles with well-developed apical teeth. Measurements: major body length 4.50 mm, head length (to apex of nasus) 1.90 mm, head width 1.11—1.13 mm, pronotum width 0.55—0.56 mm; minor body length 3.20 mm, head length (to apex of nasus) 1.32 mm, head width 0.52—0.55 mm, pronotum width 0.36—0.38 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head mainly ochre-brown, the sutures very distinct, a broad pale line on each side of the coronal suture. Postclypeus straw-yellow. Head with sparse hairs of medium length and many microtrichia; thorax and abdomen moderately hairy, the hairs mostly short. Postclypeus length slightly more than half its width. Antennae 14-segmented; segment 4 the shortest of all. Measurements: body length 4.20—4.25 mm; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.39 mm; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.73—0.77 mm; head width 1.13—1.17 mm; pronotum width 0.58—0.62 mm.
